text: C4 holds up a picture frame with ‘Scene 7’ on the back
speaker: C4

text: Scene 7
speaker: C4

text: C4 turns the frame round to reveal a picture of a theatre
speaker: C4

text: The Theatre
speaker: C4/2

text: For some reason the house was crowded that night.
speaker: C4

text: Some women were laughing in the pit.
speaker: C2

text: Their voices were horribly shrill and discordant.
speaker: C2/3

text: The manager, beaming an oily tremulous smile, escorted them to their box with a sort of pompous humility.
speaker: C1

text: What a place to find one's divinity in!
speaker: Lord H

text: Yes! she is divine beyond all living things.  When she acts, you will forget everything. These common rough people become quite different when she is on the stage.  They sit silently and watch her.  They weep and laugh as she wills them to do and one feels that they are of the same flesh and blood as one's self.
speaker: Dorian

text: The same flesh and blood as one's self!  Oh, I hope not!
speaker: Lord H

text: Don't pay any attention to him, Dorian. I understand what you mean and I believe in this girl. Any one you love must be marvellous.
speaker: Basil

text: Thanks, Basil. I knew that you would understand me. But here is the orchestra.  It is quite dreadful, but it only lasts for about five minutes.  Then you will see the girl to whom I am going to give all my life.
speaker: Dorian

text: Sibyl enters on stage - but delivers her lines listlessly. Chorus have a clock which is moved on to speed time
speaker: Stage

text: My only love sprung from my only hate! Too early seen unknown, and known too late! Prodigious birth of love it is to me, That I must love a loathed enemy
speaker: Sibyl

text: Chorus do tick tock - move hands
speaker: Stage

text: O Romeo, Romeo! Wherefore art thou Romeo? Deny thy father and refuse his name; Or, if thou wilt not, be but sworn my love, And I’ll no longer be a Capulet.
speaker: Sibyl

text: Chorus tick tock and move hands
speaker: Stage

text: O, swear not by the moon, the innocent moon, That monthly changes in her cycled orb, Lest that thy love prove likewise variable.
speaker: Sibyl

text: lights fade down
speaker: Stage

text: chorus hiss and boo
speaker: Stage

text: Henry gets up from his chair and put on his coat
speaker: Stage

text: She is quite beautiful, Dorian but she can't act. I cannot sit through another moment. Let us go.
speaker: Lord H

text: I am going to see the play through I am awfully sorry that I have made you waste an evening, Harry. I apologise to you both.
speaker: Dorian

text: My dear Dorian, I should think Miss Vane was ill. We will come some other night.
speaker: Basil

text: I wish she were ill. But she seems to me to be simply callous and cold.  Last night she was a great artist. This evening she is merely a commonplace mediocre actress.
speaker: Dorian

text: Dorian, you must not stay here any longer.  It is not good for one's morale to see bad acting.  Besides, I don't suppose you will want your wife to act, so what does it matter if she plays Juliet like a wooden doll?
speaker: Lord H

text: Go away, Harry I want to be alone.
speaker: Dorian
